MCP tools were not available. I can't give you a verified figure for Alberta's child poverty rate. I haven't retrieved the data in this session, and I won't quote a number from memory, because I can't confirm it or its vector ID.

**Where to find it:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, "Low income statistics by age, gender and economic family type". Choose:
- Geography: Alberta
- Age group: "0 to 17 years"
- Low income measure: Market Basket Measure (MBM), Canada's official poverty line
- Statistic: percentage of persons in low income

The table gives the vector ID for that selection. Under the MBM, Statistics Canada's Canadian Income Survey results are annual, and the latest reference year is usually 2023 or 2024. Check which year the table currently shows.

The rate depends on the measure. The MBM, the Low Income Measure after tax (LIM-AT) and the Low Income Cut-offs give different results, so state which one you're using.

If you'd like, I can try pulling the table directly and report the figure with its vector and reference period.

I can't give you a figure. The data tools I use to query Statistics Canada timed out or lost their connection on every attempt, so I couldn't retrieve anything. I haven't estimated a number, because I can't check one.

Statistics Canada's Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours (SEPH) is the likely source. It reports average weekly earnings by industry and province. The industry you want is NAICS 912, "Provincial and territorial public administration". I haven't confirmed which table carries it, or whether Alberta is published separately for that industry or suppressed. The tables to check are 14-10-0203-01 and 14-10-0205-01, but I haven't verified either.

If you retry in a few minutes, I can look up the table and vector and give you the latest monthly figure with its reference period. Or you can open the SEPH tables on statcan.gc.ca and filter to Alberta and NAICS 912.

The average total income of Albertans aged 15 and over was **$66,100** in 2024, the latest year available.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01, "Income of individuals by age group, gender and income source". The series is average income (excluding zeros) for total income, all ages, all genders, vector v107680657. It comes from the Canadian Income Survey.
- **Recent trend:** The average was $66,000 in 2022, $66,300 in 2023 and $66,100 in 2024. Figures are in current dollars and were released 2026-04-29.
- **Median for comparison:** The median was **$48,100** in 2024 (v107680658). The average is higher than the median because high earners pull it up, so the median is a better guide to a typical person.
- **What it covers:** This is individual income before tax. It includes government transfers, and it excludes people with zero income. It is not household income.

I can also pull household or family income, or break the figure down by age or gender, if you want.

**Alberta's median total income was $96,600 in 2024** (before tax, in current dollars). That is for economic families and persons not in an economic family combined, which is the closest Statistics Canada measure to household income.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0237-01 (Canadian Income Survey), vector v107654786. The reference period is calendar year 2024, released 2026-04-29.
- **Recent years:** The 2022 value was $96,700 and the 2023 value was $98,400. The 2024 figure is about 1.8% below 2023, before any adjustment for inflation.
- **After tax:** Median after-tax income for 2024 was $85,300 (v107654846).
- **Definition:** The table covers economic families, meaning related people living together, plus people not in a family. It is not strictly "private households". Median income for people living alone or with unrelated people is much lower than for families, so this combined figure is not the same as a family-only median.

**About 12.8% of Alberta children (under 18) were in low income in 2024.** That uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM), Canada's official poverty line. It is the latest year available.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, "Low income statistics by age, gender and economic family type". The series is v1792632015: percentage of persons under 18 in low income, MBM (2023 base), Alberta, reference year 2024.

The rate depends on which measure you use. For 2024, in the same table:

| Measure | Rate | Vector |
|---|---|---|
| MBM, 2023 base (official poverty line) | 12.8% | v1792632015 |
| Low income measure, after tax (LIM-AT) | 13.9% | v96520326 |
| Low income cut-offs, after tax (LICO-AT) | 6.1% | v96520329 |

The MBM (2023 base) rate has changed over recent years:
- 2021: 8.1%
- 2022: 12.0%
- 2023: 11.9%
- 2024: 12.8%

I did not look up the Canada-wide rate for comparison.

I couldn't find a figure for provincial public administration alone, so the closest I can give is Alberta's whole public administration sector. I couldn't get at a table that breaks out the provincial level (NAICS 912).

**Average weekly earnings, including overtime, all employees, Alberta, public administration (NAICS 91)**
- August 2026: **$1,686.48** per week, about $87,700 a year if annualized (my own calculation, ×52)
- July 2026: $1,667.00
- June 2026: $1,689.24

August and July are preliminary.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0223-01 (Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours), vector v79311410. The data are monthly and seasonally adjusted. I read it through the Statistics Canada Web Data Service.
- **Scope:** NAICS 91 covers federal, provincial, and local and Indigenous public administration together, so it isn't just provincial government workers.

Table 14-10-0205-01 reports average hourly earnings by industry. I didn't query it, so I have no hourly figure for this sector.

The average total income in Alberta was **$66,100** in 2024, the latest year available. This is the average per person aged 15 and over with income, before tax and in current dollars. It is not inflation-adjusted.

- **Median:** The median was lower, at **$48,100**, because a relatively small number of high earners pull the average up.
- **Recent years:** The average was $66,000 in 2022, $66,300 in 2023 and $66,100 in 2024.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01, "Income of individuals by age group, gender and income source." The average is vector v107680657 and the median is vector v107680658. Both are for Alberta, all ages 15+, both genders, total income. The data were released 2026-04-29 from the Canadian Income Survey.

If you meant household or family income, or after-tax income, those are in different tables. I can look those up.

Alberta's median total household income was about **$96,600** in 2024 (current dollars). This is the latest reference period available.

- **Measure:** median total income before tax, for economic families and persons not in an economic family. It includes government transfers.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0190-01 (Canadian Income Survey), vector v96414571. It was released 2026-04-29.
- **Recent trend:** the 2022 figure was $96,700 and the 2023 figure was $98,400.

I identified the vector from the table's coordinate and did not confirm the Alberta label in the response. The table doesn't report households as such, so the figure is for economic families and unattached persons combined. It is not a household-level figure. The estimates cover persons aged 15 and over.

In 2024, the latest year available, **12.8% of Alberta children under 18 were living in poverty**. This uses the Market Basket Measure (2023 base), Canada's official poverty line.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, "Low income statistics by age, gender and economic family type". The series is v1792632015 (Alberta, persons under 18, percentage in low income, MBM 2023 base). It was released 2026-04-29.
- **Trend:** The rate was 12.0% in 2022, 11.9% in 2023 and 12.8% in 2024.
- **Alternative measure:** On the after-tax Low Income Measure (v96520326), the rate was 13.9% in 2024, up from 13.5% in 2023 and 12.2% in 2022.

The two measures give different numbers because they define low income differently. I did not pull the standard error or data-quality grade for these estimates, so treat the year-to-year changes as small.

Average weekly earnings for Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration (NAICS 912) were **$1,883.03 in August 2026**. That figure includes overtime and covers all employees. It is the latest month available, and the figure is preliminary. Excluding overtime, the figure was $1,870.28.

- **Over the past year:** Earnings rose from $1,694.36 in August 2025 to $1,883.03 in August 2026, an increase of about 11%.
- **Annualized:** $1,883.03 × 52 comes to roughly $98,000 a year. That is my own arithmetic, not a published figure.
- **What the figure covers:** NAICS 912 is provincial and territorial public administration, so it covers the Alberta government's own administration. It does not include health, education or other public-sector industries. Earnings are gross payroll before deductions, in current dollars.

I did not find an hourly figure for this industry in Alberta, so I can't give one.

**Source:** Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0203-01, Average weekly earnings by industry, monthly, unadjusted for seasonality (Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours). Reference period: August 2026. The vectors are v1560358 (including overtime) and v1605659 (excluding overtime).

**Average total income in Alberta was $66,100 in 2024**, the latest year available. It is the average for people aged 15 and over who have income, before taxes, in current dollars.

- **Median:** The median was $48,100 (vector v107680658). The average is higher because a smaller number of high earners pull it up.
- **Recent years:** The average was $66,000 in 2022 and $66,300 in 2023.
- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01, "Income of individuals by age group, gender and income source". The figures are for Alberta, all ages 15+, all genders, total income, "Average income (excluding zeros)" (vector v107680657). The reference period is calendar year 2024, released 2026-04-29.

The average for people with income differs from average household or family income. I haven't looked up those figures.

**Alberta's median total income was $96,600 in 2024**, the latest year available. This is before tax and includes government transfers.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0237-01, vector v107654786. It covers economic families and persons not in an economic family, from the Canadian Income Survey. Reference period: 2024.
- **Recent trend:** $96,700 in 2022 and $98,400 in 2023. The 2024 figure is slightly lower.
- **Definition:** This table measures economic families plus individuals living outside a family. That is the closest match to "household" I found, but it isn't strictly a household measure. I didn't find a separate household-based median in the sources I checked.
- **Other income concepts:** Median after-tax income is also in this table. I didn't pull it.
